problems.reason: The holotype is dated to the middle Cenomanian to Turonian stage (mid‑Late Cretaceous), while the Paleobiology Database records Elaltitan as occurring in the Coniacian stage (earlier Late Cretaceous), giving conflicting age ranges for the same taxon.

notes: - contradiction: "The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — dates to the middle Cenomanian to Turonian stage and was collected by an expedition led by José Fernando Bonaparte." / "The Paleobi Database records the time range for Elaltitan as the Coniacian stage, from 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.": The holotype is dated to the middle Cenomanian to Turonian stage (mid‑Late Cretaceous), while the Paleobiology Database records Elaltitan as occurring in the Coniacian stage (earlier Late Cretaceous), giving conflicting age ranges for the same taxon.
